name: inputs-pane-switches-hotkey-presets
description:
Picking the Arc preset in the Inputs pane: the picker leaves Custom, the file records the NAME rather than the chords, and Cmd+T stops opening the command bar in the same run.

The pane held one user map merged over one shipped table. A preset is a named table, and what the file records is the name - so a change to Arc's chords still reaches a profile that picked Arc, and the row reset puts a row back on the SELECTED preset's chord rather than always on Atrium's. Writing every chord out as a user value would freeze the profile on today's table, which is the thing the actions:{} assertion below measures.

openCommandBar is the action under test because the two presets disagree about it in the strongest way: Atrium ships Cmd+T and Arc leaves the row unassigned (Arc's own Cmd+T is New Tab). An unassigned row in a preset is an EMPTY list, not a missing one - the native map leaves an ABSENT action on its compiled-in chord, so a missing row would keep Cmd+T bound and this scenario would pass on a build that never released the key.

THE COUNT IS THE MEASUREMENT. Cmd+T is pressed twice, once before the switch and once after, and 'command bar widget showing' must appear EXACTLY ONCE. A presence check would pass on a build where the switch never reached NativeHotkeyMap, and an absence check would pass on a build where Cmd+T never worked at all.

The fixture stages a rebound toggleSidebar so the pane opens on Custom, which is also what makes the confirm step appear: leaving Custom throws the user's own rows away and nothing in the pane remembers them.

let the docked sidebar finish rendering at the fixture's 280pt width
ssh-launched Atrium is not frontmost on a clean snapshot
park the pointer in page content, outside the sidebar column
THE BASELINE: Atrium's own preset binds the command bar here, and the count assertion needs this first opening to exist
put the command bar away before the settings window opens
open the settings window
let PushSettings' thread-pool reads land
the pane has the bound map, the shipped chords and the preset tables now

actions.expression: (() => { const item = document.querySelector('.settings-rail-item[data-pane="inputs"]'); if (!item) { return 'no inputs rail item'; } item.click(); return 'clicked'; })()

The fixture's rebound row makes the pane read Custom without anything being clicked
the row the switch is going to change, read before it changes

actions.expression: (() => { const btn = document.querySelector('.hotkey-preset[data-preset="arc"]'); if (!btn) { return 'no arc button'; } btn.click(); return document.querySelector('.hotkey-preset-question') ? 'asked' : 'sent without asking'; })()
actions.note: Leaving Custom discards the user's rows, so the pick asks first

actions.expression: (() => { const btn = document.querySelector('.hotkey-preset-confirm'); if (!btn) { return 'no confirm button'; } btn.click(); return 'clicked'; })()
actions.note: Only this second, deliberate click writes
the pick landed and NativeHotkeyMap::SetFromJSON ran on the merged view
The picker is on Arc, and no row differs from Arc any more
Arc leaves the command bar unassigned, and the row says so
The user's staged cmd+shift+j went with the confirm, and Arc's own cmd+s took the row
closes the key Settings window - the chord below must reach the browser window
let the close finish and key status pass to the browser window
re-park the pointer in the browser window's page content
THE CHANGED CHORD: Arc does not bind it, so this must reach Chromium's own new tab and leave the command bar shut
long enough that a command bar opening late would still be in the log

assertions.desc: The picker offers Arc, Atrium and Custom
A row away from the named preset reads as Custom with no click at all
the row was on Atrium's chord before the switch
Leaving Custom asks before it discards the user's rows
The confirm button is what the question offers
Arc's table reached every row, including the one it leaves unbound
The confirmed switch discarded the staged rebind

assertions.label: the-command-bar-opened-before-the-switch-and-not-after
assertions.desc: Cmd+T acted under Atrium and stopped acting under Arc, in one run - the switch reached NativeHotkeyMap with no relaunch

assertions.label: the-file-records-the-preset-name
assertions.desc: The pick survives a restart, because the name is what was written

assertions.label: the-pick-wrote-no-user-actions
assertions.desc: the chords were NOT written out as user values - a change to Arc's table still reaches this profile

assertions.label: no-unusable-argument-refusal
assertions.pattern: Atrium: the hotkeys surface sent an object the core

assertions.label: no-schema-decline
assertions.pattern: Atrium: hotkeys\.json is at a schema this build cannot

assertions.desc: liveness, and a check that the settings window really closed
